root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` allocates another f-string mode slot, `tok->tok_mode_stack_index + 1` must stay below the available `tok_mode_stack` capacity.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the crashing path, repeated single-`{` reentry preserves the active f-string depth until `tok_get_normal_mode()` reaches the next nested `f'` with `tok->tok_mode_stack_index == 199`. The vulnerable code performs `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` anyway, so the missing bound `tok->tok_mode_stack_index + 1 < MAXLEVEL` is false at the exact push site. The fixed program checks that capacity before the push and raises `too many nested f-strings` instead of selecting another slot.

nodes.state: `the_current_tok->f_string_quote = quote;` is the AddressSanitizer-reported write. It dereferences the tokenizer-mode pointer selected by the unchecked push.

`TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` preincrements `tok->tok_mode_stack_index` and returns `the_current_tok` for that selected slot. With the required bound already false, this is the violating mode-slot selection that produces the one-past-end pointer later used at the sink.

When the current f-string sees a single `{`, `tok_get_fstring_mode()` flips the current mode back to `TOK_REGULAR_MODE` and recurses into `tok_get_normal_mode()` without popping an older f-string mode, so the accumulated `tok->tok_mode_stack_index` stays live for the next nested start.

edges.relation: The exact tokenizer-mode pointer returned by `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` is the pointer dereferenced two lines later when `the_current_tok->f_string_quote = quote;` executes.
The same source-level next-slot index checked by the missing obligation becomes the actual `tok->tok_mode_stack_index` immediately after `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` preincrements the stack depth.
The stack depth that survives the single-`{` return to regular mode is the same depth observed at the next nested f-string push, showing that no pop occurred before the overflowing push site.
